question: On a fixed read from the author's existing fused-history trajectory, what changes when the fused second-newest skeleton is replaced by the very same raw skeleton from that same model state?
scope: Exploratory single-object CPU FP32; sequence 23 uses the existing no-inset crop and first automatic prompt. Other attention inputs, positions, insurance, newest memory, object pointers, decoder inputs and token counts remain identical. This tests a conditional local feature substitution, not an autoregressive full-video result.
author_mechanism: Reuse the author's fused-history path and its existing reliability weighting. During an otherwise unchanged fused replay, observe the materialized raw skeleton, author reliability result and pre-update history token; verify that the fused segment equals the author's weighted combination exactly. This observation does not introduce an inference-time gate or extra model call.
controls: In a separate fresh process reproduce the original attention and decoder tensors and binary mask exactly. Compare no-op, same-skeleton raw replacement, and a mathematically identical reconstructed-fused replacement. Preserve all position and pointer tensors and the exact key count. Record the residual fused-minus-raw magnitude, author alpha and matched source IDs. No target label may be read until every prediction is saved.
engineering: Two independent label-free seq3 observer replays must match the pinned fused-window reference masks, positional and selection traces, author memory events, and runtime trace; captured tensors and source matches must repeat exactly. Two independent fresh-process replay gates must reproduce baseline attention/decoder/masks and the reconstructed fused control, and repeat raw replacements exactly. Independently rehash and verify all outputs before using selected sequence 23 reads.
interpretation: Only the fused content is changed at fixed query and state. This does not isolate the whole model, temporal feedback, or the effect of additional frames. Author fusion includes its pre-existing reliability mechanism; no new threshold, re-detection or confidence gating is proposed. Sequence selection is retrospective and labels may be incomplete.
